subject: HealthSprint MAP - unit cost & traffic QA for pilot
messages:
From: Kate Lin <kate@healthsprint.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: HealthSprint Finance <ctr-finance@healthsprint.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T15:04:00Z
Subject: HealthSprint MAP: cost modeling & unit economics for pilot

Hi Sergio —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to formalize a short mutual action plan (MAP) for the 6-week pilot. Finance and product want visibility into unit economics so we can sign off quickly. Key asks from our side:

- Clear tokens-per-$ model and sensitivity (best/worst case)
- Assumptions on caching/prefix hit rates and how they reduce tokens consumed
- Batching impacts on both cost and latency (what batch sizes are realistic given our traffic)
- A simple acceptance gate that ties cost buckets to pilot success criteria

I've attached our high-level traffic profile for Q2 (traffic_profile_q2.csv) so you can map assumptions to realistic numbers. Can you drop a MAP draft and a short worksheet with the tokens/$ calc by Friday?

Also CC'ing finance to flag any billing questions up front.

Thanks,
Kate Lin
Director, Product
HealthSprint

Attachments: traffic_profile_q2.csv (CSV - 18KB)

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Kate Lin <kate@healthsprint.com>
Cc: HealthSprint Finance <ctr-finance@healthsprint.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: HealthSprint MAP: cost modeling & unit economics for pilot

Kate — thanks for the profile and the clear asks. Drafted a short MAP and attached a working unit-cost worksheet (HS_MAP_v0.1.xlsx and redwood_unit_cost_calc.xlsx). High-level plan below; details are in the sheet.

Summary of what I included:
- Pilot scope: 6 weeks, 3 endpoints (summary, data-extraction, triage-assistant), estimated 1.2M prompts total over pilot (per csv).
- Base model: rdm-2.7b-quant (recommended) + fallback ldm-13b for high-quality responses.
- Cost calc: tokens-per-call * calls-per-day * days => gross tokens. Multiply by tokens-per-$ (model-specific) to estimate host cost. See tab "unit_calc".
- Caching assumptions: prefix cache hit rate assumption default 40% (we can parameterize).
- Batching assumptions: safe steady-state batch size 8 for 90th pct latency under 350ms; large bursts can push batch >32 which harms tail.

Open questions for you (we made conservative defaults in the sheet):
1) Avg prompt length in tokens (you attached sample; we used 120 tokens/prompt as a starting point).
2) Target P95 latency SLO for user-facing flows (we assumed 350ms).
3) Will you accept a canary that allows 2x cost delta for first 48 hours to stabilize caching?

Next steps:
- Marissa will do an ops/traffic sensitivity sweep (small matrix) and ask for a short call to align gates.
- If the defaults look OK, we'll convert the MAP into a milestone checklist and share a DocuSign SOW-lite link for signatures.

Pls see attached. Happy to jump on a 30m tomorrow.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: HS_MAP_v0.1.xlsx (Excel - 42KB), redwood_unit_cost_calc.xlsx (Excel - 16KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Kate Lin <kate@healthsprint.com>, HealthSprint Finance <ctr-finance@healthsprint.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-29T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: HealthSprint MAP: cost modeling & unit economics for pilot

Adding a few ops-focused clarifications (inline below) — Sergio, feel free to incorporate these into the MAP sheet.

- Cache hit rate: the model-level prefix caching benefit depends heavily on how much context is shared between calls. For HealthSprint's triage-assistant, if prompts reuse the last 50 tokens as context we typically see 35-55% hit; we'll keep 45% as the mid case.

- Batching: we need to split assumptions by path:
  * Background batch (async analytic scoring): batch size 64+ is fine, cost-efficient.
  * User request path (interactive): aim for batch size 4-12 to keep P95 < 350ms.

- Warmup & cold-cache impact: expect a 12-18 hour window where per-request tokens spike as cache fills; recommend a controlled ramp (10% -> 50% traffic over 24h) or seed requests from replica logs. Put a gating item that final cost signoff should include a 48h live run to observe real cache hit.

- Tokens per dollar: our sheet calculates per-model tokens per dollar; I pushed a sensitivity tab with +/- 25% token length and +/- 30% cache hit. Please confirm if HealthSprint wants an additional "worst-case" that assumes no cache benefit.

- Acceptance gate suggestion (short):
  1) Pilot succeeds if average cost-per-conversation <= $0.08 under observed traffic AND P95 latency <= 350ms for interactive routes over the 48h live run.
  2) If cost > $0.12 or P95 > 500ms, trigger automatic rollback to smaller model and escalate to solution owner.

I'll run the sensitivity sweep today and upload results to the MAP folder.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Product Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Kate Lin <kate@healthsprint.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: HealthSprint Finance <ctr-finance@healthsprint.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: HealthSprint MAP: cost modeling & unit economics for pilot

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick answers to your open questions:

1) Avg prompt length: our analysts measured a median of ~95 tokens and 95th at ~320 tokens; we attached a small sample (api_sample.json).
2) P95 latency SLO: product will accept up to 400ms P95 for interactive, but we'd like to see 300ms if possible.
3) Canary cost tolerance: we're OK with a 2x cost risk for first 24h only if you include automated rollback thresholds.

Also: KPI note from finance — they prefer we model three cost scenarios (optimistic / base / conservative) and include an explicit line-item for fallback model egress if you need to spin up larger models for a subset of requests.

Uploading sample and will review Marissa's sensitivity output when available.

Best,
Kate

Attachments: api_sample.json (sample payloads - 8KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Kate Lin <kate@healthsprint.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: HealthSprint MAP: cost modeling & unit economics for pilot

Quick technical notes from runtime/bench perspective (pulling from our perf playbook):

- Batching behavior: steady-state batching gives good token amortization, but tail latency correlates with batch timeout and request concurrency. Recommend testing two knobs: max_batch_size and batch_latency_ms. For interactive flows, we prefer max_batch_size=12 and batch_latency_ms=20 as a starting point.

- KV/prefix cache: if you have many small unique prefixes per user, cache hit will be low. Consider deterministic prompt templates to increase reuse. Plan: run a gateway-level simulation using the attached api_sample.json to estimate expected cache-hit percentage — Marissa, can you run this in your sweep?

- Acceptance gates & experiments:
  * Experiment A: 48-hour canary at 10% traffic with cache seeding. Measure tokens/dollar and P95.
  * Experiment B: Stress test with synthetic bursts (x5 baseline) to evaluate batch-induced tail.

- Deliverable additions: I'll add a small experiment checklist and a script snippet that computes tokens per dollar from raw token logs (output to Drive link in MAP folder).

I'll drop the checklist into the MAP folder and tag the Drive link in the hubspot deal.

-Karthik
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
